```typescript
// jsPDF's built-in fonts (Helvetica, etc.) only cover the WinAnsi character
// set. If a string contains even one character outside it, jsPDF encodes the
// whole string as two bytes per character, and the font then draws each byte
// on its own: U+202A shows up as " *", U+202C as " ,", and every other
// character gets a NUL in front of it. `useFormat` adds several of these
// characters to amounts (direction marks around the currency symbol, narrow
// no-break spaces as separators), so every string has to be cleaned before
// it is handed to jsPDF.
//
// Characters are matched by code point rather than written as literals,
// because they are invisible or look like other characters, and the code
// formatter has rewritten literal curly quotes into ASCII ones before.

// The characters above U+00FF that WinAnsi still includes (its 0x80-0x9F
// range): euro, single/double low-9 and curly quotes, ellipsis, daggers,
// per mille, en/em dash, bullet, trade mark, and a few accented capitals.
// jsPDF maps these to single bytes, so they render correctly.
const WIN_ANSI_EXTRAS = new Set([
  0x20ac, 0x201a, 0x0192, 0x201e, 0x2026, 0x2020, 0x2021, 0x02c6, 0x2030,
  0x0160, 0x2039, 0x0152, 0x017d, 0x2018, 0x2019, 0x201c, 0x201d, 0x2022,
  0x2013, 0x2014, 0x02dc, 0x2122, 0x0161, 0x203a, 0x0153, 0x017e, 0x0178,
]);

// Invisible bidirectional formatting marks: LRM/RLM, the LRE-RLO embeddings
// and overrides, and the isolates. Same set `useFormat`'s `fromEdit` strips.
function isDirectionMark(code: number): boolean {
  return (
    code === 0x200e ||
    code === 0x200f ||
    (code >= 0x202a && code <= 0x202e) ||
    (code >= 0x2066 && code <= 0x2069)
  );
}

// No-break space and narrow no-break space; an ordinary space looks the same
// in a PDF.
function isNonAsciiSpace(code: number): boolean {
  return code === 0x00a0 || code === 0x202f;
}

const MINUS_SIGN = 0x2212;

// Iterates by code point, so an emoji (a surrogate pair) is handled as one
// character and becomes a single '?'.
export function toPdfSafeText(text: string): string {
  let result = '';
  for (const char of text) {
    const code = char.codePointAt(0) ?? 0;

    if (isDirectionMark(code)) {
      continue;
    }

    if (isNonAsciiSpace(code)) {
      result += ' ';
    } else if (code === MINUS_SIGN) {
      result += '-';
    } else if (code <= 0xff || WIN_ANSI_EXTRAS.has(code)) {
      result += char;
    } else {
      // Emoji, the rupee sign, non-Latin scripts: '?' keeps one unsupported
      // character from garbling the rest of the string.
      result += '?';
    }
  }
  return result;
}
```

```typescript
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';

import { expect, test } from './fixtures';
import { ConfigurationPage } from './page-models/configuration-page';
import { Navigation } from './page-models/navigation';

// Every string drawn in the PDF, in drawing order. jsPDF doesn't compress
// its content streams by default, so text is stored as `(escaped text) Tj`.
function pdfTextStrings(pdf: Buffer): string[] {
  const raw = pdf.toString('latin1');
  return [...raw.matchAll(/\(((?:\\.|[^\\)])*)\) Tj/g)].map(match =>
    match[1].replace(/\\([()\\])/g, '$1'),
  );
}

test.describe('Budget month PDF export', () => {
  let page: Page;

  test.beforeEach(async ({ browser }) => {
    page = await browser.newPage();
    const configurationPage = new ConfigurationPage(page);

    await page.goto('/');
    await configurationPage.createTestFile();

    // The stray characters only appear when a currency is set: that's when
    // the amounts carry invisible direction marks around the symbol.
    const settingsPage = await new Navigation(page).goToSettingsPage();
    await settingsPage.waitFor();
    await settingsPage.settings
      .getByRole('button', { name: 'None', exact: true })
      .first()
      .click();
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'USD - US Dollar ($)' }).click();
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Budget', exact: true }).click();
  });

  test.afterEach(async () => {
    await page?.close();
  });

  test('downloads a readable PDF of the budget month', async () => {
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export budget month' }).click();

    const menu = page.getByRole('menu');
    const singleMonthItem = menu.getByRole('button', { name: 'Export as PDF' });
    // With one month on screen the menu has "Export as PDF"; with several,
    // the PDF section comes last, so its last item is always a PDF month.
    const pdfItem = (await singleMonthItem.isVisible())
      ? singleMonthItem
      : menu.getByRole('button').last();

    const downloadPromise = page.waitForEvent('download');
    await pdfItem.click();
    const download = await downloadPromise;

    expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toMatch(/\.pdf$/);

    const pdf = await readFile(await download.path());
    expect(pdf.subarray(0, 5).toString('latin1')).toBe('%PDF-');

    const strings = pdfTextStrings(pdf);

    // AC6: "<Budget name>: <Month YYYY>"
    expect(strings[0]).toMatch(/^.+: [A-Z][a-z]+ \d{4}$/);
    // AC7: "Page N of M" footer
    expect(strings.some(text => /^Page 1 of \d+$/.test(text))).toBe(true);
    // AC1: amounts print as "$1,234.56" / "-$45.00"
    expect(strings.some(text => /^-?\$\d{1,3}(,\d{3})*\.\d{2}$/.test(text))).toBe(
      true,
    );
    for (const text of strings) {
      // A NUL means jsPDF fell back to two-byte encoding, which the
      // built-in font draws as stray characters.
      expect(text).not.toContain('\u0000');
      expect(text).not.toContain('*');
    }
  });
});

```

```mts
// Vitest config for mutation testing the PDF export fixes (issue #97) with
```

```markdown
# Mutation testing: Issue #97 -- Improve PDF export formatting/data view

**PR(s):** #TODO  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.0.0 (command runner; see [Setup notes](#setup-notes))  **Config:** [`packages/desktop-client/stryker.issue-97.config.json`](../../../packages/desktop-client/stryker.issue-97.config.json), [`vitest.stryker.issue-97.config.mts`](../../../packages/desktop-client/vitest.stryker.issue-97.config.mts) and [`vitest.stryker.issue-97.setup.ts`](../../../packages/desktop-client/vitest.stryker.issue-97.setup.ts), based on Bennett Matuszewski's setup from #163  **Command:** `cd packages/desktop-client && npx stryker run stryker.issue-97.config.json`
**Reports:** [before](reports/97-tigerk9-before.json) · [after](reports/97-tigerk9-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 75.15% → after 90.53%

|        | Mutants | Killed | Timed out | Survived | Score  |
| ------ | ------- | ------ | --------- | -------- | ------ |
| Before | 169     | 127    | 0         | 42       | 75.15% |
| After  | 169     | 153    | 0         | 16       | 90.53% |

| File                    | Before  | After   |
| ----------------------- | ------- | ------- |
| `pdfText.ts`            | 85.71%  | 100.00% |
| `budgetMonthPdfRows.ts` | 100.00% | 100.00% |
| `budgetMonthPdf.ts`     | 59.26%  | 80.25%  |

**What was mutated.** The three source files the PR changes in `packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/export/`: `pdfText.ts` (new: cleans text so jsPDF's built-in font can draw it), `budgetMonthPdfRows.ts` (row shape: one Category column, separate Total and To Budget types) and `budgetMonthPdf.ts` (table layout, styles, "Page N of M"). The PR's only other source change is the one-line PDF title in `BudgetExportMenu.tsx`, a React component that the unit tests don't render, so I left it out. The tests run are the three PDF test files plus `budgetMonthCsv.test.ts`, which guards AC8 (the CSV export must not change).

## Setup notes

- **Command runner, as in #163.** The Vitest runner (`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.0.0) runs no tests for any mutant with Vitest 5, so every mutant "survives". Bennett documented this in [125-bennettmatuszewski.md](125-bennettmatuszewski.md). I used his workaround: Stryker's command runner starts Vitest once per mutant (`--bail 1 --maxWorkers 1`).
- **Separate config files.** I added `stryker.issue-97.config.json` and `vitest.stryker.issue-97.config.mts` instead of editing Bennett's, so his command still reproduces his report.
- **Two additions to the standalone Vitest config:**
  - The shared row walk (`budgetMonthRows.ts`) imports `MonthsContext.tsx`, so the config compiles JSX (`oxc: { jsx: { runtime: 'automatic' } }`). Without it, the CSV and row tests fail to load.
  - `vitest.stryker.issue-97.setup.ts` initializes i18next. The regular test run initializes it indirectly (`setupTests.ts` → mocks → redux store → i18n). Without it, `t('Total')` returns `undefined` and 16 tests fail before Stryker starts. I checked that all 57 (before) and 73 (after) tests pass under this config before each run.
- **Timeouts.** My first after run used `concurrency: 4`. It reported 4 mutants in `budgetMonthPdf.ts` (lines 114–117) as timed out, which Stryker counts as detected (92.90%). They had survived the before run, and two of them are equivalent (see the table), so the timeouts were the machine being overloaded, not tests catching them. I reran at `concurrency: 2` and they survived with no timeouts. The after report and score above are from that run, and the committed config uses 2. The before run had no timeouts at 4.

## Questions

<!-- DRAFT: rewrite these answers in your own words before submitting. -->

**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**

My first tests checked *what* the PDF says but not much about *where or how* it says it. The text checks were solid: `budgetMonthPdfRows.ts` was already at 100% and every amount-formatting mutant was killed. But several tests passed for the wrong reason. The "never splits a row" check used one-line rows, which can't straddle a page break anyway. The page-number check found "Page 1 of 2" in the file without checking it was on the page. The style test checked that the four row types differ, not *how*, so dropping Total's border still passed because bold kept the rows different. The `pdfText.ts` survivors showed I had only tested the characters `useFormat` produces today, not the full set the issue's design says to strip. I left the title and footer font gaps open on purpose: no AC specifies fonts, and a test that pins jsPDF's internal font numbers would be brittle.

**2. Did any survivor expose an assertion whose expected value wasn't based on the requirements?**

No assertion had a wrong expected value, but one test was weaker than its requirement. The AC7 test was named "repeats the header", yet it only checked the "Budgeted" header, so any of the other three could have been blank (lines 127/129/130). AC7 says the *column header row* repeats, so the fixed test checks all four header texts on every page. Separately, while writing the tests the code formatter rewrote `’` into an ASCII `'` in both the input and the expected value of one test. That test "passed" while checking nothing about the apostrophe-dot format. I found it by scanning the files for non-ASCII characters, and changed the tests to build those characters from code points (`String.fromCharCode(0x2019)`).

**3. AI use, and what was verified or corrected.**

I used Claude Code (Opus 5.5) to set up the Stryker config, run both passes and draft the survivor table; the session is logged in [ai-logs/sprint3/tigerk9/](../../../ai-logs/sprint3/tigerk9/) (TODO: link the specific file). I checked the classifications rather than taking them on trust. Each "equivalent" claim about a library default was confirmed with a small script against the real jsPDF/autotable: default font size 16, 40pt margins, default cell styles, `'auto'` width, and Times as the fallback for an unknown font. That last check changed lines 116/162 from "equivalent" to "gap". The 4 timeouts in the first after run were rerun at lower concurrency rather than counted as kills, which lowered the reported score from 92.90% to 90.53%.
```

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`

```text
## 2. PR

**Title:** `[AI] feat: add Update VRT screenshots workflow (#153)`
**Milestone:** Sprint 3 _(doesn't exist yet — needs to be created; only "Sprint 2" is open)_
**Reviewer:** **[Liam]** pick a teammate you haven't had review you yet this semester

### Description

Upstream's `/update-vrt` comment bot can't run in our fork (its jobs are limited to
`actualbudget/actual` and need Depot runners), and screenshots made in our arm64 dev containers
don't match CI. The only working way to update VRT screenshots was copying a temporary workflow
into the PR (#116). This PR adds a permanent **Update VRT screenshots** workflow that anyone can
start from the Actions tab with a PR number.

- **`.github/workflows/update-vrt.yml` (new).** Checks the PR is open and from this repo, builds it
  and runs VRT with `--update-snapshots=changed` in CI's container (`playwright:v1.61.1-jammy`,
  same build steps as `e2e-test.yml`), then pushes one commit with only the changed PNGs and starts
  E2E Tests on it. Optional "Test files" input runs only those files in one shard. The jobs that run
  the PR's code only get a read-only token; the job that pushes never runs PR code and re-checks
  that every file is a PNG in a `*-snapshots` folder.
- **`e2e-test.yml`:** `workflow_dispatch` trigger, so the workflow can start the checks on its commit.
- **`e2e-vrt-comment.yml`:** replaces "comment `/update-vrt`" with step-by-step instructions and
  the failed test files, read from the VRT JUnit reports by `.github/scripts/vrt-failed-files.mjs`.
- **`fork-ci-guard.yml`:** also runs the tests in `.github/scripts` (lage only runs workspace tests).
- **`STUDENTS.md`:** new "Updating VRT screenshots" section.
- Release note.

AI disclosure: written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5); see the AI Assistance comment for the log.
**[Liam]** add what you reviewed/changed yourself.

### Design decisions

The issue's Design section (icsasso) chose a new `workflow_dispatch` workflow over adapting
upstream's `/update-vrt`. These are the decisions I made while implementing it.

**1. How the checks run on the bot's screenshot commit**

- **Decision:** after pushing, the workflow starts E2E Tests on the PR branch itself with
  `workflow_dispatch`, which needed a `workflow_dispatch:` trigger in `e2e-test.yml`.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  1. _Re-run the old VRT check by hand_ (the issue's original AC 3). Doesn't work: a re-run tests
     the same commit as the original run, so it tests the old screenshots.
  2. _Push an empty commit or close and reopen the PR by hand._ Works and changes no upstream file,
     but every person has to remember an extra step after each update.
  3. _A personal access token secret_ so the bot's push starts CI. Needs a repo admin to create
     and rotate a token tied to one person's account.
- **Rationale:** `workflow_dispatch` is the one event GitHub lets `GITHUB_TOKEN` start, so it needs
  no secret and no manual step. The cost is three lines in one upstream file.
- **Consequences:** _Easier:_ the checks start on their own after an update. _Harder:_ one more
  upstream edit that can conflict at syncs; branches made before this merges can't be started this
  way (the workflow warns and says to merge `master`); and GitHub still holds the other PR checks
  for approval, so E2E can run twice.

**2. Which job gets write access**

- **Decision:** split the workflow so the jobs that build and run the PR's code (`build-web`,
  `generate`) have a read-only token, and only the `commit` job can push. It never runs PR code: it
  re-checks the downloaded files are PNG screenshots, then commits and pushes.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  1. _One job that runs the tests and pushes_ (like #116's temporary workflow). Simpler, but the
     PR's code would run with a token that can push to any branch.
  2. _Upstream's two-workflow design_ (generate a patch, then a separate `workflow_run` workflow
     applies it). Same separation, but two files, and `workflow_run` workflows can only be tested
     after they're on `master`.
- **Rationale:** keeps the separation upstream uses, in one file that could be tested on a fork
  before merging.
- **Consequences:** _Easier:_ a broken or malicious test can't push anything but screenshots.
  _Harder:_ screenshots move between jobs as artifacts, and the PNG check runs in two places.

### Related issue(s)

Closes #153

### Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- Two upstream workflow files are edited (`e2e-test.yml` trigger, `e2e-vrt-comment.yml` message and
  steps). They can conflict at upstream syncs; the edits are marked "Fork-only (issue #153)".
- After a bot commit, E2E runs twice: once started by the workflow, once when someone approves the
  held PR checks.
- Screenshots are made from the PR branch as it is, while PR checks test the branch merged with
  `master`. If `master` changed screenshots in the meantime they can differ; `STUDENTS.md` says to
  merge `master` first.
- An E2E run started by the workflow doesn't get a VRT Comment if it fails (the comment only runs
  for `pull_request` runs). The red check is still visible on the PR.
- The `.github/scripts` tests add a job (~1–2 min) to the Fork CI guard workflow.
- The tests read the workflow files with a small helper (`.github/scripts/read-workflow.mjs`)
  instead of a YAML library, so no dependency is added. It only understands our workflows' layout;
  if that changes in a way it can't read, the tests fail rather than pass.

**Encountered:**

- Upstream's `/update-vrt` workflows can't run here; replaced rather than adapted (issue Design).
- `budget.test.ts:466` ("switches to the mobile layout below the small breakpoint") is flaky: it
  failed (both tries) in an E2E run on the test fork's bot commit, but passed one commit earlier and
  passed on this PR. The bot's commit only changed 3 PNGs, which Functional tests don't read
  (`toMatchThemeScreenshots` is a no-op without `VRT`). Not changed here; reported as #___
  **[Liam: file the bug and fill in]**.
- Pre-existing shellcheck notes in `e2e-test.yml` / the comment's "Extract metadata" step left as is.
```

```markdown
# Draft for issue #97: rewrite in your own words before posting

Lines marked **[Liam]** need your input. Everything below the line is the PR body to paste.

**Title:** `[AI] feat: improve PDF export formatting (#97)`
**Milestone:** Sprint 3
**Reviewer:** **[Liam]** pick a teammate

---

## Description

The budget-month PDF export from #60/#61 printed stray `*` and `,` characters in amounts, repeated the category group name on every row, and cut off large totals. This PR fixes those and makes the PDF easier to read.

**Cause of the stray characters.** `useFormat` wraps the currency symbol in invisible direction marks (U+202A/U+202C), and some formats use a narrow no-break space (U+202F). jsPDF's built-in Helvetica only covers the WinAnsi character set. When a string contains even one character outside it, jsPDF encodes the *whole* string as two bytes per character, and the font draws each byte separately: U+202A becomes ` *`, U+202C becomes ` ,`, and every other character gets an invisible NUL in front of it. The NULs widen the text, which is also why large totals wrapped and got cut off. Turning the fix off makes the "fits on one line" test fail as well, which confirms both symptoms have the same cause.

**Changes** (`packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/export/`):

- **`pdfText.ts` (new):** `toPdfSafeText()` cleans every string before it goes into the PDF. It removes direction marks, turns U+00A0/U+202F into a normal space and U+2212 into `-`, and replaces any other character the font can't draw with `?`.
- **`budgetMonthPdfRows.ts`:** one `label` column instead of separate Category Group / Category columns, so each group name appears once, on its bold row (Design Decision 2). `grandTotal` is split into `total` and `toBudget` so they can be styled differently, and the never-used `groupSubtotal` type is removed. The data still comes from the same row walk the CSV export uses.
- **`budgetMonthPdf.ts`:**
  - 4 columns, with fixed-width, right-aligned money columns (fit `-$1,234,567.89`) and a Category column where long names wrap
  - grayscale styles per row type: indented categories, shaded group rows, a top border on Total, and To Budget shaded with a top border
  - a dark header row repeated on every page, and rows never split across pages
  - a "Page N of M" footer
  - `renderBudgetMonthPdf()` is split out so tests can inspect the laid-out table
- **`BudgetExportMenu.tsx`:** the title is now `<Budget name>: <Month YYYY>` (AC6).
- **Tests:** new `pdfText.test.ts`, rewritten `budgetMonthPdf.test.ts`, updated `budgetMonthPdfRows.test.ts`, and a new E2E test `e2e/budget-export.test.ts`.
- **Mutation testing:** `stryker.issue-97.config.json`, `vitest.stryker.issue-97.config.mts` and `.setup.ts` (based on Bennett's #163 setup), plus the write-up `docs/sprint3/mutation/97-tigerk9.md` with its before/after reports.
- Release note.

### Differences from the issue spec

- **New `pdfText.ts` file.** The Rough Scope named only `budgetMonthPdf.ts` and `budgetMonthPdfRows.ts`. The cleanup function lives in its own file so it can be unit-tested and mutation-tested on its own.
- **`?` for characters the font can't draw.** This goes beyond Design Decision 1, which only strips or replaces the characters `useFormat` adds. Without it, a single emoji or ₹ in a category name garbles the *whole* cell, because jsPDF switches the entire string to two-byte encoding. Non-Latin text is still out of scope; it now degrades to `?` instead of garbage.
- **Also touched:** the one-line title change in `BudgetExportMenu.tsx` (needed for AC6), and a new E2E test file.

## Related issue(s)

Closes #97

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- **The `?` fallback.** ₹ and non-Latin category names (Cyrillic, CJK, emoji) print as `?`. Fixing that properly means embedding a Unicode font, roughly 150–300 KB, which the issue puts out of scope.
- **The cleanup is tied to `useFormat`.** `toPdfSafeText` handles the characters `useFormat` adds today. If it starts adding a new invisible character outside WinAnsi, that character will print as `?` until it's added to `pdfText.ts`.
- **The tests read text from the PDF's raw content.** They rely on jsPDF writing uncompressed content (its default). If someone turns compression on, those tests will fail rather than pass silently.
- **A second Stryker config.** There are now two configs in `desktop-client` (#125's and this one).

**Encountered:**

- **`groupSubtotal` was dead code.** It was a `PdfRowType` that was never produced; removed.
- **The code formatter changes test characters.** `oxfmt` rewrote `’` (the curly apostrophe used by the apostrophe-dot format) into a plain ASCII `'` in both a test input and its expected value, so that test passed while checking nothing. It did the same to the source's list of drawable characters, which would have printed `’` as `?`. Fixed by building those characters from code points (`String.fromCharCode(0x2019)`). **[Liam]** worth a team note: anyone writing tests with special characters can hit this.
- **Bennett's Stryker setup needed two additions for these files.** JSX compilation, because the shared row walk imports `MonthsContext.tsx`, and an i18next init. Both are added in the new config files; his files are unchanged.
- **Typecheck and lint under lage fail in the dev container.** `yarn typecheck` fails the web workspace with no error printed, and `yarn lint` crashes (`tsgolint` SIGPIPE), while the same steps pass when run directly (see CI / commands). This looks environmental (memory); not changed here.

- **Where the expected values come from:** the ACs (`$1,234.56`, `-$45.00`, `-$1,234,567.89`, `My Budget: November 2026`, "Page N of M"), Settings' number format labels, and the issue's Design section. None were copied from the code's output, and the inputs are the exact strings `useFormat` produces, written by hand.
- **Checking the tests catch the bug:** with `toPdfSafeText` replaced by a function that returns its input, 3 PDF tests fail, including the AC4 one-line test.
```

Base directory for this skill: /workspaces/actual-budget/.claude/skills/committing-actual-changes

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.
